premise: The humble beginnings of a Delta blues legend who played on street corners before recording hits.
hook: He worked as a tractor driver in Mississippi cotton fields while earning coins by singing gospel and blues on street corners.
key_facts: Worked on a cotton plantation in Indianola, Mississippi, during his youth.
Traveled to Memphis, Tennessee, seeking a radio break, eventually working as a disc jockey known as the Beale Street Blues Boy.
Named his signature Gibson electric guitars 'Lucille' after an incident involving a tavern fire.
Recorded dozens of influential blues standards over a decades-long touring career.

premise: A college dropout builds a computer in his parents' garage with his friend during the 1970s tech boom.
hook: Before building iPhones, he dropped out of college, slept on friends' floors, and built circuit boards in a garage.
key_facts: Dropped out of Reed College after attending for one semester
Co-founded Apple Computer in 1976 inside a suburban garage
Traveled to India seeking spiritual guidance prior to starting Apple

premise: His grueling decade training at the China Drama Academy as a child.
hook: Before he broke box office records, he trained for 19 hours a day under a master who promised teachers could break their bones.
key_facts: Enrolled in the Beijing Opera School (China Drama Academy) at age six by his parents.
Trained rigorously in martial arts, acrobatics, singing, and acting for ten years.
Worked as a stuntman and extra in Bruce Lee films before landing leading roles.

premise: A young chess prodigy in India sharpens his lightning-fast tactical skills in local clubs.
hook: Before becoming a world champion, he earned the nickname 'Lightning Kid' for his rapid moves.
key_facts: Became India's first Grandmaster in 1988
Won multiple World Chess Championships across different formats
Awarded India's highest civilian sporting honor, the Padma Vibhushan

premise: A routine bus ride in Montgomery, Alabama sparks a historic boycott.
hook: One quiet refusal on a crowded city bus triggered a 381-day movement that changed history.
key_facts: Worked as a seamstress and NAACP secretary.
Refused to surrender her bus seat on December 1, 1955.
Her arrest catalyzed the Montgomery bus boycott.

premise: A struggling actor with partial facial paralysis refuses to sell his script unless he plays the lead.
hook: He was so broke he had to sell his dog for $50 just to buy food—then wrote a blockbuster script in three days.
key_facts: Experienced complications at birth leading to speech and facial nerve issues.
Lived in extreme poverty and slept in the New York Port Authority bus terminal.
Refused multiple studio offers to buy the Rocky script without him starring.

premise: A messy laboratory bench leads to the accidental discovery of the world's first antibiotic.
hook: A stray mold spore drifted through an open window and accidentally destroyed a scientist's experiment.
key_facts: Noticed a Petri dish of Staphylococcus bacteria contaminated by Penicillium mold in 1928.
Published findings on penicillin in the British Journal of Experimental Pathology.
Shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1945.

premise: An orphaned daughter of emancipated slaves builds a nationwide haircare enterprise.
hook: She started by mixing formulas in a wash tub and became America's first self-made female millionaire.
key_facts: Born on a cotton plantation in Delta, Louisiana, in 1867.
Developed a line of African American hair care products.
Employed thousands of women as sales agents across the United States.

premise: A television actor makes a contract choice that changes his career trajectory.
hook: He turned down top billing on a famous TV show because he wanted his name listed alphabetically instead.
key_facts: Starred in the 1960s television sitcom Gilligan's Island.
Requested his character's name appear fourth in the opening credits sequence.
Served in the United States Army during the Korean War.

premise: A young engineering student in Karnal looks at pictures of planes and dreams of spaceflight.
hook: She grew up in a small town where local girls rarely pursued aviation, yet she ended up working at NASA.
key_facts: Graduated with a degree in aeronautical engineering from Punjab Engineering College.
Obtained a Ph.D. in aerospace engineering from the University of Colorado Boulder.
Joined NASA's astronaut corps in 1994.

premise: An Antarctic expedition crew survives months on floating ice after their ship is crushed.
hook: Their ship was completely crushed by pack ice, stranding 28 men in the freezing Antarctic for over a year.
key_facts: Led the Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition aboard the Endurance in 1914.
Navigated an open lifeboat 800 miles across the Southern Ocean to South Georgia Island.
Successfully rescued every member of his crew without a single loss of life.

premise: A university closure forces a young scholar to retreat to his family farm to ponder physics.
hook: A university plague shutdown sent him home, where a falling fruit sparked a breakthrough in gravity.
key_facts: Studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, until it closed due to the Great Plague of London.
Developed foundational theories on calculus, optics, and motion during his rural isolation.
Published Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica in 1687.
